scope: One additional living marine specimen for the species guide, optional identification practice and reef encounters. Copy is newly paraphrased. Biology uses museum accounts and an explicitly cautious diet inference in a government synthesis coauthored by Australian Museum researchers. Observation instructions are prompts, not claims that every behavior is simulated.
iucnYearConvention: iucnYear is the assessment year, matching existing fish metadata. Assessed 28 June 2016; the assessment was published in the 2016 Red List and an errata version was published in 2017. The IUCN specialist group's current table still labels the latest assessment 2016. specimens.name: Banded pipefish (ringed pipefish)
specimens.iucnCitation: Pollom, R. 2016. Dunckerocampus dactyliophorus (errata version published in 2017). The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2016: e.T6814A115083653.
marks: Very slender, elongated body with a long, narrow tubular snout
Alternating pale and red-to-black bands cross the head and body
A distinct reddish tail fin ends the thin body
White margins line the tail fin above and below, with one or more pale spots near its centre
specimens.role: Thought to prey on tiny crustaceans in sheltered reef habitats; its detailed wild feeding role is poorly documented.
specimens.fact: In this relative of seahorses, the male broods the developing eggs.
specimens.habitat: Sheltered tropical western Pacific reefs and lagoons, especially caves, crevices and spaces beneath ledges.
specimens.diet: Its detailed wild diet is poorly documented; it is thought to take tiny crustaceans, like other pipefishes.
specimens.behavior: Often found as a pair near shelter; it may also occur alone or in small groups. It can hover in recesses beneath reef ledges.
specimens.observe: Trace the long snout, then follow the alternating bands to the tail. Look for the pale tail margins and central spot or spots.

claimSupport.marks: dx-am-banded_pipefish for long snout, transverse bars and distinct caudal fin; dx-foa-banded_pipefish and dx-lkc-banded_pipefish for tail colour, pale margins and central spots; dx-foa-order-syngnathiformes for general tubular snout and elongate pipefish body
claimSupport.roleDiet: dx-ea-banded_pipefish explicitly states that the species' diet is unknown and small-crustacean feeding is an inference from its family; retain the uncertainty in both role and diet copy. dx-foa-order-syngnathiformes supports the family/order-level small-crustacean predation pattern, not a measured diet for this species.
claimSupport.fact: dx-foa-banded_pipefish quick facts: males brood eggs; dx-foa-order-syngnathiformes supports seahorse relationship and developing-embryo brooding. Do not infer a sealed pouch or modeled sex.
claimSupport.habitat: dx-foa-banded_pipefish for current western Pacific range, sheltered reefs/lagoons/caves/crevices; dx-lkc-banded_pipefish and dx-ea-banded_pipefish for reef ledges
claimSupport.behavior: dx-lkc-banded_pipefish for alone/pairs/small groups; dx-ea-banded_pipefish for usually paired adults and hovering beneath ledges
claimSupport.iucnCitationPublishedErrataYear: dx-mnhn-banded_pipefish; dx-iucn-ssg-banded_pipefish lists latest published assessment 2016; dx-cas-banded_pipefish notes IUCN 2017

specimens.caution: DD means insufficient information to assess extinction risk, not that the species is secure. The accepted genus is Dunckerocampus; Doryrhamphus dactyliophorus appears in older sources. FoA warns that older records can include the similar D. naia or D. boylei, so current museum western Pacific distribution is preferred over an unqualified broad Indo-Pacific range. Tail spots vary (FoA usually 1–3), and bands may be red through nearly black. No existing guide organism is a genuine close visual lookalike. Do not assign a confirmed cleaner role, universal pair bond, precise wild prey list, coiled prehensile tail, or sealed seahorse-like brood pouch. The 2002 synthesis has old conservation advice and distribution; use it only for explicit diet uncertainty, male egg attachment and hovering behavior, not current status.

modelProvenance.nominalAdultLengthBasis: An illustrative 17 cm adult, slightly below the 18 cm maximum in Australian Museum and current Museums Victoria accounts. Seed variation is illustrative, not a measured size distribution.
modelProvenance.depthChoice: FoA quick-facts species range 5–56 m is retained for consistent metadata. Its prose says usually shallow protected reefs/caves to about 10 m, and a Singapore museum field record is shallower than 1 m; 5 m is not a biological lower boundary. The guide should avoid presenting the metadata interval as exhaustive.
modelProvenance.anatomy: Narrow elongated angular body, very long thin tubular snout, tiny fins and a distinct reddish caudal flag. Pale/red-to-black transverse bands extend over the head and snout. Caudal fin has white dorsal/ventral margins and usually 1–3 central pale spots; do not assume one invariant exact spot shape. FoA gives head length 3.7–4.6 in standard length, snout length 1.4–1.8 in head length, snout depth 10.6–20.8 in snout length. These are proportions, not exact target millimetres.
modelProvenance.motion: A restrained hovering presentation near sheltered reef structure is supported. Fine fin motion and small local flex are artistic teaching choices, not measured kinematics. Avoid a pronounced moray-like body wave, seahorse tail coil, or school animation. Existing organisms must retain their positions and seeds.
modelProvenance.sexBrooding: The educational fact concerns real male brood care. The model need not depict a male or brooding eggs; do not present an opaque closed pouch as diagnostic anatomy.
